Selected work
Lead and CRM automation

Arabic lead intake, qualification and follow-up

A personal portfolio demo for a fictional physiotherapy business, with Telegram intake and a CRM dashboard.

  • Node.js
  • TypeScript
  • Telegraf
  • OpenRouter
  • Google Apps Script
Demo Personal portfolio build Where this number comes from

The problem

A clinic gets enquiries at every hour, most of them outside the hours anyone is at a desk. Reception handles them when it can, in between the people physically standing in front of them. Every message that waits until tomorrow is a booking that may not happen, and none of it is recorded anywhere afterwards.

What it does

01

Answers in the patient's language

Conversational intake in Arabic, which is what the people messaging this clinic actually write. A polished English bot would have been useless here.

02

Qualifies while it talks

It asks what it needs, scores the enquiry, and routes the ones worth a human straight to the team instead of into a queue.

03

Keeps the thread

Follow-ups fire on their own, and every conversation is tracked on one dashboard, so the enquiry exists somewhere other than in a phone.

How it is built

InboundQualifyRouteFollow upDashboard

Node.js and TypeScript over the Telegram Bot API, with the language model behind OpenRouter and Apps Script carrying the sheet-side of the demonstration CRM.

What I'd watch if it were yours

Speed to first reply beats sophistication

Most of the value here is answering at all, quickly. The qualification is the second-order win.

Build in the language of the person typing

Dialect intake is not a nice-to-have in this market, it is the difference between a system that gets used and one that gets ignored.

Start with operations the demo can show

The dashboard, follow-up flow and intake history provide an example of how a team would review leads.

The demo uses the fictional SmartFlow / MoveWell clinic scenario. Source and setup are public at github.com/Moamen-Elsharkawy/leadsync-ai.
